@TomColeOK04 Cuts today, not tomorrow.

I don’t necessarily disagree with you on this. The work program is a good idea in theory, but has left a lot to be desired in actual practice. 

I’d like to hear what is different than what was done in Arkansas and Georgia where more people lost coverage due to bureaucratic BS than actually not meeting the requirements. 

The Congressional Budget Office estimates that this is going to cut off coverage for 13 million people by 2034. How many of those people are going to lose their coverage even though they’re still eligible?

That’s not fear mongering, that’s asking important questions to protect your constituents.

Democrats love screaming about Medicaid cuts to distract from their own failures. The real issue? Medicaid is riddled with fraud and bureaucratic bloat. Instead of fearmongering, let’s target the waste: overpriced contracts, administrative fat, and endless red tape that siphon billions from taxpayers.

Reform isn’t about slashing care—it’s about redirecting funds from D.C. grift to actual patients.

But don’t expect honesty from a party that profits off broken systems.
